rationale: Correct ACES Delta's owner roster by removing the unsupported treatment of GIC, OTPP and AIMCo as direct owners. Those institutions, together with Manulife, invested as limited partners in Haddington ESP I. Current direct platform ownership is held through Chevron-controlled Magnum Development as majority owner and Mitsubishi Power Americas as minority owner. Haddington's former indirect platform ownership ended when Chevron acquired Magnum in 2023; Haddington's separately managed ACES I construction equity remains project-level context rather than a direct ACES Delta platform ownership period.

beforeImage.name: ACES Delta
beforeImage.description: ACES Delta is a large-scale clean hydrogen production and storage project in Delta, Utah. Its target end markets include long-duration power storage and industrial decarbonization applications that require dispatchable low-carbon hydrogen. The project is asset-heavy and development-oriented, with economics tied to electrolysis, salt-cavern storage, and long-duration energy infrastructure rather than to a conventional merchant generation asset. U.S. Department of Energy materials state that the facility combines 220 MW of alkaline electrolysis with two 4.5 million barrel salt caverns capable of supporting long-duration storage. The reviewed materials did not disclose project-level revenue or GIC's ownership percentage within the broader equity syndication consortium. Public materials show that DOE closed a US$504.4 million loan guarantee in 2022 and that GIC participated through a Haddington-led equity financing program around the project.

DOE closed a US$504.4 million loan guarantee for the project.
Public reporting indicated Chevron had acquired a majority stake in ACES Delta from Haddington Ventures.

afterImage.name: ACES Delta, LLC
afterImage.description: ACES Delta, LLC is a clean-hydrogen production and underground salt-cavern storage platform in Delta, Utah. The 2019 joint venture is currently owned by Chevron-controlled Magnum Development, LLC as majority owner and Mitsubishi Power Americas, Inc. as minority owner; exact percentages are not publicly disclosed. Haddington Energy Partners III formerly owned the platform indirectly through Magnum and exited that position when Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum in 2023. Haddington ESP I separately manages construction equity in the ACES I project company, while GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife are investors in that fund rather than verified direct ACES Delta owners. The first stage comprises 220 MW of electrolysis and two salt caverns supporting more than 300 GWh of storage. All 40 electrolyzers were reported commissioned in the first quarter of 2026, with final start-up still expected later in 2026. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.
